issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree concerning immovable property that was the subject matter of the suit is exempt from compulsory registration when no collusion is alleged.
material_facts: A court had issued a compromise decree declaring rights in land that was the subject matter of the original suit.
The decree was later objected to when it was tendered in evidence, on the ground that it had not been registered.
No allegation was made that the decree was collusive.
The lower courts held registration necessary, relying in part on the view that a title claimed through adverse possession could not have existed before the decree.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree did not require registration and was admissible in evidence; the orders holding otherwise were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act, 1908 generally requires registration of instruments affecting rights in immovable property, but Section 17(2)(vi) exempts court decrees except compromise decrees comprising immovable property outside the subject matter of the suit or proceeding. Bhoop Singh v. Ram Singh Major explains that a collusive compromise or one creating rights for the first time may require registration; Som Dev v. Rati Ram confirms that a compromise decree concerning property within the suit does not require registration. The reasoning based on Gurdwara Sahib v. Gram Panchayat Village Sirthala was no longer valid because Ravinder Kaur Grewal v. Manjit Kaur overruled it and held that perfected adverse possession can support a claim as well as a defence.

rule.if: civil_appeal_challenges_registration_ruling and decree_is_court_compromise and decree_property_within_original_suit and no_collusion_alleged

predicates.civil_appeal_challenges_registration_rul: A party appeals a ruling that a decree cannot be admitted because it was not registered.
predicates.decree_is_court_compromise: A court issued the decree on the basis of a compromise.
predicates.decree_property_within_original_suit: The immovable property covered by the decree was the subject matter of the original suit or proceeding.
predicates.no_collusion_alleged: No party alleges that the decree was collusive.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a registration ruling concerning a court-issued compromise decree over property that was part of the original suit, and no collusion is alleged, the decree does not require registration.
